- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic spikes in forecast after recent highs — cap upward revisions at +3% of prior 7-day average.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and forecast deviates >1.5σ from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over last 3 forecasts, add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to correct lagged underestimation.  
- If sentiment shows sudden spike (e.g., >0.8) followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
